transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-10
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miller (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Ruiz (Aurora CTO), Sam Park (Aurora ML), Maya Chen (Aurora SRE)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm jordan from redwood, and priya is our solutions engineer. can you hear us ok?
[00:07] Dr. Elena: yes, loud and clear. thanks. we've been looking at inference platforms for our clinical summarization pipeline. latency is the biggie for us.
[00:15] Jordan: great, that's exactly what we wanted to dig into today — p95 targets, concurrency, streaming behavior, tokens per second, and then recommendation whether Hosted, Dedicated, or Private makes sense.
[00:25] Priya: quick agenda — gather current workload, target p95, token lengths, concurrency, streaming usecases, security constraints, then recommend an approach and next steps. sound good?
[00:33] Dr. Elena: yep. to give context, our main path is ingesting notes and returning a structured clinical summary and suggested codes. typical prompt length is 400-800 tokens, we have some short alerts at ~100 tokens. p95 we want under 300ms for the short path and under 700ms for the longer 800 token summarizations — that's tight i know.
[00:53] Sam: concurrency varies, baseline ~20 concurrent inference calls during business hours, spiky to 80 for overnight batch processing. but the real-time UI needs the low p95 for the short alerts.
[01:05] Maya: also, we stream partial results into the UI as they arrive — streaming is mandatory for the clinician experience.
[01:12] Priya: ok, couple clarifying q's — are you doing streaming tokens as chunks streaming, or full-chunk streaming? and are you willing to tolerate slightly higher p50 if p95 is stable?
[01:23] Dr. Elena: we stream token chunks to the UI, user sees incremental summary. p95 is the metric for our SLO, if p95 is above threshold clinicians complain. p50 can float.
[01:34] Jordan: got it. can you share your current infra — are you self-hosting models or using an API today?
[01:40] Sam: currently using a hosted inference provider and a custom LLM for clinical summarization. cost is climbing and latency is inconsistent. we're evaluating three paths: keep Hosted but optimize, Reserved/Dedicated capacity with predictable throughput, or Private (VPC/on-prem) because of PHI concerns.
[01:55] Priya: from experience, for streaming p95 at 200-300ms on short prompts you typically need either a dedicated lower-latency tier or a hosted plan with guaranteed capacity and prefix caching. private on-prem can help but often adds network overhead unless you're colocated.
[02:10] Dr. Elena: interesting — can you explain caching/prefix behavior? sometimes our prompts have long shared instructions.
[02:16] Priya: sure — we do KV/prefix caching so repeated system prompts or common context doesn't re-run heavy compute. that reduces token/sec compute for tail requests. batching also helps throughput but can hurt p95 if you wait to fill batches. Redwood offers continuous batching with policies tuned to p95 SLOs.
[02:33] Jordan: also worth highlighting routing and fallback — if Dedicated is at capacity we can route to a warm Hosted fallback with slightly different model variant to keep latency bounded.
[02:43] Maya: how do you measure tokens/sec in a streaming scenario? our engineering team needs to benchmark end-to-end not just the model.
[02:51] Priya: good q. recommended approach: run synthetic load with your request distribution, measure end-to-end p50/p95, and measure tokens/sec generated during streaming. we provide a benchmark harness (we'll share the spreadsheet) with sample workloads and post-processing scripts.
[03:05] Sam: our SRE cares about concurrency and autoscale — what's the expected concurrency capacity for a single Dedicated pool e.g., for a T4- or A10-class GPU?
[03:13] Priya: capacity depends on model size and quantization; e.g., a 7B quantized model on A10 can do ~150-300 tokens/sec depending on sequence length and perf knobs. smaller prompts with streaming will have lower per-request latency. for high concurrency (20-80) you'd typically use a pool with multiple GPUs and a batching policy.
[03:30] Dr. Elena: p95 targets we mentioned — short 100 token path at <300ms, longer 800 token at <700ms — are those realistic?
[03:38] Priya: short path at <300ms is aggressive but achievable with Dedicated + warm KV cache + streaming-first config. Hosted can hit it during stable load if you buy reserved capacity. Private can also but depends on your network and infra.
[03:49] Jordan: we should set realistic benchmark steps — start with single-user streaming tests to validate p95, then ramp concurrency to 20, 50, 80 while measuring p95 and tokens/sec. Priya will outline the script.
[04:02] Priya: action items: we'll provide the harness and recommended config (batching windows, prefer-latency vs prefer-throughput flag, quantization recommendation).
[04:10] Dr. Elena: on security, we need SOC 2, SSO/SAML for RBAC, KMS for keys, and VPC peering for Private. if we go Hosted, data residency and audit logs required.
[04:20] Jordan: we can provide SOC2, we support SAML SSO and KMS integrations, and Dedicated/Private gives you more network isolation and control over keys. we'll attach the compliance pack.
[04:28] Maya: one more thing: in our infra we want to avoid cold starts — how do you handle warm pools and burst capacity?
[04:34] Priya: Dedicated supports configurable warm pools and burst capacity. for Hosted we have soft reservations and burst options; cold starts can be mitigated by auto-warming and prefix caching.
[04:42] Sam: what about model variants and graceful degradation? we sometimes are okay with a smaller model at higher load as long as results degrade gracefully.
[04:49] Jordan: yes, smart routing can fallback to a smaller, quantized variant, and we can label rollouts to A/B test quality. we'll measure quality regressions with your evals.
[04:58] Dr. Elena: ok, timeline — we want to run a POC in two weeks; initial success criteria are: short-path p95 <300ms at concurrency 20, streaming intact, and <= X cost per 1M tokens (we need your pricing ballpark).
[05:12] Priya: we'll provide a benchmark plan and sample configs. Jordan will follow up with pricing ranges for Hosted reserved, Dedicated commitment tiers, and Private licensing.
[05:20] Jordan: recap of next steps: send benchmark harness and spreadsheet, SOC2 and security docs, sample Dedicated pricing and example pool configs, and schedule a benchmarking session.
[05:29] Dr. Elena: perfect. one small note — sometimes transcriptions miss product names. we mean Redwood Dedicated / Redwood Private.
[05:35] Jordan: thanks, noted. any final q's?
[05:38] Maya: none from me.
[05:40] Sam: nothing else.
[05:41] Dr. Elena: thanks everyone, looking forward to the harness.
[05:44] Jordan: thanks all, we'll send the materials today and set the follow-up. bye.

Notes on quality: some words may be auto-transcribed incorrectly (e.g., 'kv cache' as 'kay vee cash' etc.). Shared artifacts: benchmark harness spreadsheet (link provided in follow-up), SOC2 and compliance pack, Dedicated pricing PDF.
